highlights.title: Fix DynamicISF crash when autosens min is 1
changes: Fixes a crash when DynamicISF uses the sigmoid option and autosens minimum is set to 1.
The sigmoid calculation now nudges the minimum value so sensitivity ratios adjust with glucose instead of causing an -∞.
As a result, Swift's oref behavior differs from the JavaScript version for this specific edge case.

highlights.title: Suspend/Resume button fixed
changes: The Suspend/Resume button now works correctly in the app.

includedPullRequests.title: Fixes numerical issue with DynamicISF
includedPullRequests.body:
If DynamicISF is using sigmoid and has a autosensMin value == 1 then
there are numerical issues with log10 returning -Inf, causing a crash
loop (https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/issues/1441).

The fix is to add a fudge factor to avoid this case, similar to what
JS oref had for a divide by zero when autosensMax == 1.

Important: This change will cause Swift's oref to behave differently
from JS. JS will simply default to a ratio of 1 for all cases when
autosesnsMin == 1, with this (very hacky) fix the Swift implementation
will product ratios that adjust as glucose changes (see unit tests).

Moving forward we should strongly consider replacing sigmoid with a
straight line -- they just aren't that different in practice and a
straight line is much easier to implement and understand, which is a
big deal given two hacks to work around numerical issues and some
random 0.0555 in the algorithm. But that will be for a future PR.
